side_notes: All three agents operated almost entirely at the sentence/clause level (length, notation density, appositive glosses, front-loaded qualifiers, metaphor). No finding examines paragraph-level structure: ordering of the five U-paragraphs, whether the scope-disclaimer repetition is a paragraph-architecture problem rather than a per-sentence one, or transitions between paragraphs. The repeated-disclaimer finding (a2-f4) is the closest to a cross-paragraph observation but is still framed as wording redundancy.

Coverage skews heavily to section2.2-U1 (the notation/setup paragraph). U2-U5 are touched, but no finding looks at U4's two-sentence 'different clocks' unit as a whole vs. its parts, nor at whether later paragraphs inherit complexity from U1's dense setup.

Materiality grading is internally consistent within the style frame but uncalibrated against reader impact: every 'major' is a length/density/meta-commentary cluster and every 'minor' is a single-device observation. No finding attempts to weight which device most raises parse load for the non-specialist target reader, so the human reviewer has no ranking beyond the major/minor binary.
